intro: Martial arts rooms have their own clothes. Judo students wear a thick jacket. Sumo wrestlers wear a wide belt. School wrestlers in Illinois wear a one-piece suit.
In this unit, you will learn what a belt shows. You will learn that a belt is a mark of rank, not magic. You will also learn the names of many arts and the places they come from.
By the end, you can name a uniform and tell which art wears it. You can tell karate from taekwondo. You can find Okinawa, Korea, China, Thailand, Brazil and Europe in each name.
bigQuestion: What can clothes and names tell us about where a martial art comes from?

The name taekwondo is chosen in Korea

write.prompt: Pick two martial arts from this unit. Tell where each one comes from and what its students wear. Use at least two dates or records from the unit, such as 1882 for judo or 1955 for taekwondo. Tell one way the two arts are the same and one way they are different.
tips: Name the place each art comes from.
Use one date for each art.
Use words from the unit, like judogi, dobok or singlet.
Tell what a belt or uniform shows, not what it does.

title: Jacket and Belt

chapters.title: A School Mark
chapters.bigQuestion: What do the clothes and belts in a martial arts room tell people?

story.title: Books on a Shelf
story.kicker: A jacket and a belt can tell a story, like a library book.
paragraphs: A small room has a wooden shelf by the door. On the shelf sits a white jacket, folded flat. A long cotton belt lies on top of it. The belt is orange.
The jacket and belt wait in a row, like books in a library. Each book has a label that tells where it goes. The belt is a label too. It tells which class a student is in.
The belt is not magic. It does not make anyone strong or fast. It is a mark the school gives. It shows how long a student has studied and what the teacher says they know.
Other rooms use other clothes. Fencers dress in white. Wrestlers in Illinois wear a one-piece suit. Each room picks clothes that fit its own rules.
story.think: What clothes or marks show which group you are in at school?

lessons.title: The Judo Jacket
lessons.mainIdea: Judo students wear a thick cotton jacket and pants called a judogi.
reading: Kanō Jigorō started *judo* in Tokyo, Japan, in 1882. His school was called the Kodokan. His students needed strong clothes for class.
They wore a thick cotton jacket and loose pants. This outfit is called a *judogi*. Gi means clothes. The jacket is heavy so it does not rip easily.

words.d: a sport from Japan, started by Kanō Jigorō in 1882
the thick cotton jacket and pants worn for judo

look.title: A Heavy Jacket
look.text: Look at a white jacket hanging on a hook. The cloth is thick, like a towel. The sleeves are wide. A belt hangs beside it.
look.prompt: Why might a school want its jackets made of thick cloth?

check.q: Who started judo?
check.why: Kanō Jigorō started judo in Tokyo in 1882.

check.q: What is a judogi?
choices: the jacket and pants worn for judo
check.why: The judogi is the cotton jacket and pants for judo.

check.q: What was Kanō's school called?
check.why: Kanō's judo school in Tokyo was the Kodokan.

lessons.title: Karate Takes a Jacket
lessons.mainIdea: Karate teachers in Tokyo began to wear a jacket like the judo jacket.
reading: *Karate* grew on the island of Okinawa. In the 1920s, karate teachers brought it to Tokyo. One teacher was Funakoshi Gichin.
In Tokyo, karate students began to wear a white jacket, pants and belt. It looked a lot like judo clothes. Today it is called a *karategi*. It is often lighter than a judogi.

words.d: a martial art that grew on the island of Okinawa
the white jacket, pants and belt worn for karate

look.title: Two Jackets
look.text: Look at two white jackets side by side. One is thick and heavy. That one is for judo. One is thinner and lighter. That one is for karate.
look.prompt: How are the two jackets the same? How are they different?

check.q: Where did karate grow?
check.why: Karate grew on the island of Okinawa.

check.q: Which clothes did karate students wear in Tokyo?
choices: a white jacket, pants and belt
check.why: In Tokyo, karate students wore a white jacket, pants and belt, much like judo.

check.q: Who was one karate teacher in Tokyo in the 1920s?
check.why: Funakoshi Gichin brought karate from Okinawa to Tokyo.

lessons.title: White Belt, Black Belt
lessons.mainIdea: A belt is a mark of rank that a school gives; it is not magic.
reading: In the 1880s, Kanō Jigorō gave his students ranks. He called the top ranks *dan*. Students with a dan rank wore a black belt. New students wore white.
A belt shows a *rank*. A rank is a step in a school. The belt does not give power. It shows what the teacher says the student has learned.

words.d: a step or level in a school
a top rank in judo and other arts; people with a dan rank often wear a black belt

look.title: Two Belts on a Hook
look.text: Look at two belts on a hook. One is white and stiff and new. One is black. The black belt belongs to a student who has studied for many years.
look.prompt: What does the black belt tell you about the student? What does it not tell you?

check.q: What does a belt show?
check.why: A belt is a mark of rank. It is not magic.

check.q: What color belt did Kanō's dan students wear?
check.why: In Kanō's school, dan students wore black belts.

check.q: What color belt did new students wear?
check.why: New students in Kanō's school wore white belts.

lessons.title: Colors Come Later
lessons.mainIdea: Many colored belts came later, and schools use different color orders.
reading: At first, judo had few belt colors. In the 1930s, a judo teacher in Paris used more colors. His name was Mikinosuke Kawaishi. He wanted students to see each step.
Many schools now use a *color belt* for each step. Yellow, orange, green and blue are common. But the order is not the same everywhere. Each school or group picks its own.

words.d: a belt of one color that shows one step in a school
which thing comes first, next and last

look.title: Two Charts on Two Walls
look.text: Look at a chart on one school wall. It goes white, yellow, orange, green. Now look at a chart in a different school. It goes white, yellow, green, blue.
look.prompt: Why can the same color mean a different step in two schools?

check.q: Where did Kawaishi teach judo?
check.why: Mikinosuke Kawaishi taught judo in Paris in the 1930s.

check.q: Is the belt color order the same in every school?
choices: no, each school picks its own
check.why: Schools and groups pick their own order of colors.

check.q: What does one color belt show?
check.why: A color belt shows one step in a school.

lessons.title: A Rope for a Sumo Champion
lessons.mainIdea: In sumo, the belt and a white rope show a wrestler's rank.
reading: Sumo wrestlers in Japan wear a wide belt called a *mawashi*. It wraps around the waist. Wrestlers wear it in every match.
The top rank in sumo is *yokozuna*. At special times, a yokozuna wears a thick white rope around his waist. The rope shows everyone his rank.

words.d: the wide belt a sumo wrestler wears
the top rank in sumo

look.title: A Thick White Rope
look.text: Look at a big wrestler walking into a hall. A thick white rope is tied around his waist. Paper strips hang from the front. The crowd knows his rank at once.
look.prompt: How does the rope help the crowd?

check.q: What is a mawashi?
check.why: The mawashi is the wide belt sumo wrestlers wear.

check.q: What is the top rank in sumo?
check.why: Yokozuna is the top rank in sumo.

check.q: What does a yokozuna wear at special times?
check.why: A yokozuna wears a thick white rope that shows his rank.

lessons.title: The Wrestling Singlet
lessons.mainIdea: School wrestlers in Illinois wear a one-piece suit called a singlet.
reading: Wrestlers at school do not wear a jacket or belt. They wear a *singlet*. A singlet is a tight suit made in one piece. It is easy for a referee to see.
In Illinois, high school wrestling is run by the *IHSA*. Boys first had state champions in 1937. Girls had their first state finals in 2022.

words.d: a tight one-piece suit worn for wrestling
the Illinois High School Association, which runs high school sports in Illinois

look.title: Illinois Years
look.prompt: How many years after the boys did girls have state finals?

check.q: What is a singlet?
check.why: A singlet is a tight one-piece suit for wrestling.

check.q: When did Illinois girls have their first state wrestling finals?
check.why: IHSA girls wrestling held its first state finals in 2022.

check.q: Who runs high school wrestling in Illinois?
check.why: The IHSA runs high school sports in Illinois.

lessons.title: White for Fencing
lessons.mainIdea: Fencers wear white clothes and a mask with a metal screen.
reading: Fencing grew in Europe. Fencers wear white jackets and pants. They also wear a *mask*. It has a metal screen over the face.
Long ago, judges watched for touches with their eyes. White clothes helped them see. Later, electric wires helped judges score. They were used at the Olympics in 1936.

words.d: a fencing helmet with a metal screen over the face
a sport from Europe where two people score touches with blades

look.title: All in White
look.text: Look at two fencers on a long strip. Both wear white from neck to knee. Both faces are hidden behind dark metal screens. A wire trails behind each one.
look.prompt: What do the white clothes and wires help the judges do?

check.q: What color do fencers wear?
check.why: Fencers wear white jackets and pants.

check.q: Where did fencing grow?
check.why: Fencing grew in Europe.

check.q: What helped judges score at the 1936 Olympics?
check.why: Electric wires helped judges score fencing at the 1936 Olympics.

review.q: What does a belt show in a martial arts school?
review.why: A belt is a mark of rank that the school gives.
Judo students wear a thick cotton judogi.

review.q: What do school wrestlers in Illinois wear?
review.why: School wrestlers wear a one-piece singlet.

review.q: Who used more belt colors in Paris in the 1930s?
review.why: Kawaishi used more colors so students could see each step.

review.q: Which art brought a white jacket to Tokyo in the 1920s?
review.why: Karate teachers from Okinawa began wearing a white jacket in Tokyo.

review.q: What does a yokozuna's white rope show?
review.why: The white rope shows the yokozuna, the top rank in sumo.

chapters.title: Many Names
chapters.bigQuestion: Why does each martial art have its own name and its own home?

story.title: Six Names on a Sign
story.kicker: A hallway sign lists six arts, and each one comes from a different place.
paragraphs: A long hallway has a sign on the wall. The sign lists six classes. Judo. Karate. Taekwondo. Kung fu. Muay Thai. Capoeira.
The names do not match. They come from different languages. Judo and karate are Japanese words. Taekwondo is a Korean word. Muay Thai is a Thai name. Capoeira is a word in Portuguese.
Each name points to a home. Judo began in Tokyo. Karate grew in Okinawa. Taekwondo comes from Korea. Kung fu comes from China. Muay Thai comes from Thailand. Capoeira comes from Brazil.
People sometimes mix these names up. But each art has its own story. Learning the names is a way to learn where people and their arts come from.
story.think: Which of the six names have you heard before? Where did you hear it?

lessons.title: Judo Means Gentle Way
lessons.mainIdea: Judo is a Japanese name that means the gentle way.
reading: Judo is a Japanese word. Ju means gentle. *Do* means way. So judo means the gentle way.
Kanō Jigorō chose the name in 1882 in Tokyo. Many other arts also end in do. Karate-do and taekwondo end with a word for way.

words.d: a word that means way, found at the end of many art names

look.title: Split the Name
look.text: Look at the word judo on a card. Cut the card in two. One half says ju, which means gentle. The other half says do, which means way.
look.prompt: What other names end in do?

check.q: What does do mean in judo?
check.why: Do means way. Judo means the gentle way.

check.q: What does ju mean?
check.why: Ju means gentle.

check.q: Where did Kanō choose the name judo?
check.why: Kanō Jigorō named judo in Tokyo in 1882.

lessons.title: Karate from Okinawa
lessons.mainIdea: Karate grew in Okinawa, once the kingdom of Ryukyu, and its name means empty hand.
reading: Okinawa is an island south of Japan's main islands. It was once part of a kingdom called *Ryukyu*. Japan took over the kingdom in 1879.
People in Okinawa practiced an art often just called te, or hand. In the 1930s, teachers chose to write karate as empty hand. Kara means empty. Te means hand.

words.d: an old kingdom on Okinawa and nearby islands
an island south of Japan's main islands, where karate grew

look.title: An Island on a Map
look.text: Look at a map of the sea near Japan. A long chain of small islands stretches south. The biggest one is Okinawa. Boats once sailed from there to China and Japan.
look.prompt: Why is it more exact to say karate comes from Okinawa, not just Japan?

check.q: What was the old kingdom on Okinawa called?
check.why: Okinawa was part of the kingdom of Ryukyu.

check.q: What does karate mean?
check.why: Kara means empty and te means hand.

check.q: When did Japan take over the Ryukyu kingdom?
check.why: Japan took over the Ryukyu kingdom in 1879.

lessons.title: Taekwondo from Korea
lessons.mainIdea: Taekwondo is a Korean art, and its name was chosen in 1955.
reading: *Taekwondo* comes from Korea. The name was chosen in 1955. Tae means foot. Kwon means fist. Do means way.
Taekwondo students wear a white uniform called a *dobok*. Its home office, the Kukkiwon, is in Seoul. Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

words.d: a martial art from Korea; the name was chosen in 1955
the white uniform worn for taekwondo

look.title: Three Parts
look.text: Look at the word taekwondo on a card. Cut it in three. Tae means foot. Kwon means fist. Do means way.
look.prompt: Which part of taekwondo is the same as the end of judo?

check.q: Where does taekwondo come from?
check.why: Taekwondo comes from Korea.

check.q: When was the name taekwondo chosen?
check.why: The name taekwondo was chosen in 1955.

check.q: What is a dobok?
check.why: The dobok is the uniform worn for taekwondo.

lessons.title: Karate Is Not Taekwondo
lessons.mainIdea: Karate and taekwondo are two different arts from two different places.
reading: Karate and taekwondo both use white uniforms and belts. So people sometimes mix them up. But they are two different arts.
Karate grew in Okinawa. Its room is called a *dojo*. Taekwondo comes from Korea. Its room is called a *dojang*. Each word comes from its own language.

words.d: the Japanese word for a room where an art is practiced
the Korean word for a room where taekwondo is practiced

look.title: Two Doors
look.text: Look at two doors side by side. One sign says karate dojo. The other sign says taekwondo dojang. Behind both doors, students wear white.
look.prompt: What is the same behind the two doors? What is different?

check.q: What is a taekwondo room called?
check.why: A taekwondo room is called a dojang.

check.q: Where did karate grow?
check.why: Karate grew in Okinawa. Taekwondo comes from Korea.

check.q: Why do people sometimes mix up karate and taekwondo?
choices: both use white uniforms and belts
check.why: Both use white uniforms and belts, but they are different arts.

lessons.title: Kung Fu Is a Big Word
lessons.mainIdea: Kung fu is a wide English word for many Chinese martial arts.
reading: China is a very big country. It has many martial arts, not just one. In English, people often call them all *kung fu*.
In Chinese, kung fu means skill that comes from hard work and time. A cook or a painter can have kung fu too. Another Chinese word for martial arts is *wushu*.

words.d: a wide English word for many Chinese martial arts; in Chinese it means skill from hard work
a Chinese word for martial arts

look.title: One Word, Many Arts
look.text: Look at a big umbrella. Under it stand many people from all over China. Each one learned a different art from a different teacher. The umbrella says kung fu.
look.prompt: Why is kung fu like a big umbrella?

check.q: What does kung fu mean in Chinese?
choices: skill from hard work and time
check.why: In Chinese, kung fu means skill that comes from hard work and time.

check.q: How many martial arts does China have?
check.why: China has many martial arts, not just one.

check.q: What is another Chinese word for martial arts?
check.why: Wushu is a Chinese word for martial arts.

lessons.title: Muay Thai from Thailand
lessons.mainIdea: Muay Thai is the boxing of Thailand, and its name means Thai boxing.
reading: *Muay Thai* comes from Thailand. Muay means boxing. So Muay Thai means Thai boxing. It is a national sport there.
Fighters in Muay Thai often wear a headband called a *mongkon*. They take it off before the match begins. Music plays during a match in Thailand.

words.d: the boxing of Thailand; the name means Thai boxing
a headband worn by Muay Thai fighters before a match

look.title: A Headband
look.text: Look at a fighter stepping into a ring in Bangkok. A stiff round band sits on the fighter's head. A teacher lifts it off before the match starts.
look.prompt: What does this headband tell you about which art this is?

check.q: What does muay mean?
check.why: Muay means boxing. Muay Thai means Thai boxing.

check.q: What is a mongkon?
check.why: The mongkon is a headband worn by Muay Thai fighters.

check.q: Where does Muay Thai come from?
check.why: Muay Thai comes from Thailand.

lessons.title: Fencing Words from France
lessons.mainIdea: Many fencing words are French, and the world fencing group began in Paris.
reading: Fencing grew in Europe. Many of its words are French. Piste means the strip. Touché means touched.
In 1913, fencing groups met in Paris. They made a world group called the *FIE*. Its rule words are often still in French.

words.d: the world group for fencing, made in Paris in 1913
a French word that means touched

look.title: Words on a Card
look.text: Look at a word card by a fencing strip. It says piste, which means strip. It says touché, which means touched. Both words are French.
look.prompt: Why might a sport keep words from one language?

check.q: What does touché mean?
check.why: Touché is French for touched.

check.q: Where was the FIE made?
check.why: The FIE was made in Paris in 1913.

check.q: What language are many fencing words in?
check.why: Many fencing words are French.

lessons.title: Names at the Olympics
lessons.mainIdea: Different arts joined the Olympics in different years.
reading: The Olympics bring sports from many countries together. Fencing was in the first modern Games in 1896. Judo joined in 1964 in Tokyo.
Taekwondo became an Olympic medal sport in 2000 in Sydney. Karate was in the Games held in Tokyo in 2021. Each name joined in its own year.

words.d: big Games where people from many countries meet

look.title: First Olympic Year
look.unit: year of first Olympic medal event
look.prompt: Which art joined the Olympics first? Which joined last?

check.q: When did judo join the Olympics?
check.why: Judo joined the Olympics in Tokyo in 1964.

check.q: Which art was in the first modern Games in 1896?
check.why: Fencing was in the first modern Olympics in 1896.

check.q: Where did taekwondo become an Olympic medal sport?
check.why: Taekwondo became a medal sport in Sydney in 2000.

review.q: What is kung fu in English?
choices: a wide word for many Chinese arts
review.why: Kung fu is a wide English word for many Chinese martial arts.
Dojang is the Korean word for a taekwondo room.
Muay means boxing, so Muay Thai means Thai boxing.

review.q: When was the FIE made in Paris?
review.why: The world fencing group, the FIE, was made in Paris in 1913.
